# Mixed fallback descriptors and physical adapters

We complete the fallback instruction descriptors left open by PR2188 and
connect them to PR2171's physical controlled ADD. We assume completed
weighted reversed children with the contract in section 3. We prove the
composed endpoint and retain their recursive cost. We do not prove the
entire selected supplier, its finite invoice or the multiplication theorem.

Ross Richardson's PR2159 supplies the fallback algorithm, covariance and
conservative child allowance. Commdata2338's PR2188 supplies mixed
diagonal-pair descriptors and their recursive evaluator. Jose Manuel's
PR2171 supplies the sequential ADD and preparation-sensitive estimate.
We reuse those results. Our new part retains intermediate row labels for
every shear, binds their physical indices and inverse chronology, passes
generated descriptors to children, and executes complete small programs.

## 1. Quantified interface

Fix an odd prime q and w>=1; write R=Z/q^w. Let M be an invertible
N-by-N matrix over R, N=2m, with determinant +1 or -1. M acts independently
on f>=1 logical atom columns. The selected application has m=64 and

    M = [[I-P, P C_m], [C_m P, I-C_m P C_m]],
    P = g diag(0_22,I_42) g^-1.

This is the selected idle child 6, unhosted copy 213. The verifier binds it
to the retained template, the word receipt and the selected assembly's
Git-blob citation. The charts in our fixtures are GL implementation charts;
we do not present them as emitted orthogonal-cover invocations. PR2195
provides the separate whole-call local-ring integration argument.

At logical column j, let

    M_j = B_j M B_j^-1,
    B_j = diag(b_0(j),...,b_(N-1)(j)),
    b_i(j) = A[i f+j] for i<m, and 1 for i>=m.

Assume A has a finite Root/Good/FallbackPair descriptor of the forms in
PR2188. It reads only exposed ancestor fields and fixed labels. M reads
the full current matrix header. Neither may read active address values,
payload bits or the unused descendant row field U. We compute the prepared
plans from full headers; we do not supply pivot or ancestor-weight oracles.

The payload may contain arbitrary correlated bits at the complete addresses.
All intervening and trailing spectators remain complete. For an incoming
head width n, take f=floor(n/m), retain the first mf head atoms and their
corresponding reversed tail atoms, and treat the peeled atoms as spectators.
The code covers coordinate-projector ancestor labels and the named good
normal form. Binding further local-frame labels is a remaining compiler task.

Under the completed-child, preparation and boundary hypotheses below, our
program implements M_j at every column, fixes U and the spectators, and
returns closed adapter work. It retains all zero shear and identity-pair
slots. At m=64 it uses at most the inherited 98,682 children, each of width
at most f, within the selected charge 131,072.

## 2. Intermediate permutations and inverse order

Run unnormalized unit-pivot elimination on M. At pivot k, choose the first
unit row at or below k, swap it into position k, then clear the other N-1
rows. Retain zero coefficients as instructions. Over a local ring an
invertible remaining block has a unit in its first column, so this process
reaches a unit diagonal D.

Track pi_t(i), the original row at position i after t operations. For each
column j the retained covariance invariant is

    T_t^(j) = B_t(j) T_t B_0(j)^-1,
    B_t(j) = diag(b_(pi_t(i))(j)).

A row swap S remains an unweighted swap: update pi and B_t by conjugating
with S. For a clearing shear i <- i+c_t k, use

    c_t(j) = c_t b_(pi_t(i))(j) / b_(pi_t(k))(j).

This preserves the invariant. Both divisors are units, while c_t(j) may be
zero or a nonzero nonunit. Unit diagonal multiplication preserves which
entries are units, so the pivot itinerary is independent of ancestor
weights. The low current matrix determines that itinerary. Full-ring
coefficients and incoming weights still require their high parts.

At termination the diagonal entry is

    d_i(j) = d_i b_(pi_final(i))(j) / b_i(j).

Only this formula uses the final permutation. Our compiler attaches the
current pi_t to each shear before advancing the itinerary. It applies the
diagonal first, then inverse row operations in reverse chronological order.
For an inverse shear, negate its recorded coefficient and retain its
recorded permutation. This gives M_j because

    O_T^(j) ... O_1^(j) M_j = D_j.

The product of weighted diagonal entries equals the unweighted product:
the numerator and denominator weights permute the same multiset. Realize
each pair (i,N-1) with scales d_i(j),d_i(j)^-1, then apply the remaining
fixed determinant sign on field N-1. The sign is independent of j.

For a counterexample to final-permutation substitution, use the genuine
rank-one bad residual over Z/9 from PR2159:

    M = [[7,6,3,3], [8,3,7,1], [1,7,3,8], [3,3,6,7]].

Our mixed ancestors generate A=[1,5]. The first unweighted clearing step
is ADD(1,0,4). The correct weighted coefficient is 2. A later swap gives
pi_final=[0,2,1,3]; substituting it early gives 4. In the weighted matrix,
entries (1,0),(0,0) are 4,7. The correct clearing gives 4+2*7=0 modulo9;
the wrong one leaves 5. We also compare the reconstructed full operator.

## 3. Physical indices and recursive children

Write sigma_i(t)=t on a head field and f-1-t on a tail field. Physical atom
t in field i represents logical column j=sigma_i(t). The source atom for a
shear from field k is sigma_k(j). Evaluate c_t(j) at that logical column.

If i>k, the target field follows the source field, so the retained ordered
ADD applies. If i<k, execute J_1 on fields i,k, then the ordered ADD targeting
k from i, then J_1 again. The middle ADD must use the orientation of its
actual target k. Keep the coefficient's original row labels i,k and pi_t;
only its physical column lookup changes.

For the selected modulus25, f=3 example, elimination slot16088 clears
row42 using row126. Its inverse shear has logical coefficients [21,21,16].
After the two-swap lowering, the middle ADD targets tail126 and therefore
needs physical coefficients [16,21,21]. Using the original head42
orientation gives the wrong physical payload. Our two-operand stream test
checks this operation on 32,500 bits with unused stock and a middle field.

The completed child contract is

    F_a(H,D) = (diag(a) C_f D, C_f diag(a)^-1 H).

It acts on two complete blocks, retains exposed controls and complete
spectators, restores its row field pointwise, and closes its work at the
specified origins. It also needs the locality and uniform time contract
in section 5. We charge its full logical volume and width.

A logical weighted swap J_a between fields of opposite orientations is one
F_a. Between equal orientations, execute R_later F_a R_later. Each reversal
is an unweighted reversed child on the first and last floor(f/2) atoms;
leave a possible middle atom fixed. For f=1 no reversal child is needed.
A diagonal pair is J_1 followed by J_(d_i(j)). Its weighted child receives
the existing FallbackPair descriptor, with reverse=(i>=m). Unweighted row
swaps, conversion swaps and reversal children receive a unit Root descriptor.
Thus these calls remain in the existing mixed descriptor grammar.

We emit all N(N-1) shears and N-1 diagonal pairs, including zero and identity
slots. At most N row swaps occur. Charging three reversed children for any
ordinary weighted swap gives the inherited conservative bound

    6 N(N-1) + 3 N + 6(N-1) = 98682, for N=128.

We retain that bound even though particular fixtures use fewer children.
We do not claim a numerical supplier improvement from this observation.

## 4. Sequential adapters and preparation

For a later-target atom ADD, view the complete stream as

    exposed parents | U and earlier fields | X | middle | Y | suffix.

The coefficient evaluator reads only the exposed parent descriptor. We use
PR2171's split/merge routine to move the record at Y to Y+cX modulo q^w.
Earlier address fields can join the loop's unused prefix because the
coefficient does not inspect them. The source and target positions remain
complete q^w fields; the middle and suffix retain their full ranges.

The evaluator accepts c=0 and nonunits. Each invocation retains its slot and
charge. It resets and erases split work before the next operation. Our fixed
sign adapter retains the Y=0 block and reverses the other block order with
two sequential stack passes that preserve the bits inside each block.
It costs O(V) per atom and uses no weighted child.

Let S_l be the suffix volume of an ordered shift and F_l=V/(q^w S_l) the
number of complete target fibres. Let E_l include full-header access,
ancestor evaluation, modular arithmetic, descriptor preparation and resets.
The retained estimate is

    T_adapters <= C N_slots V + 2 sum_l F_l E_l
               <= N_slots V (C + 2 E_max/q^w).

Here N_slots=O(m^2 f), with m fixed. We do not infer a time theorem from
Python operation counts. The fixture meter measures payload accesses and
cleanup; it does not include the completed-child implementation or the
entire controller arithmetic.

Each Good node requests one older weight; each FallbackPair requests at
most two. A shear requests two such weights. At depth D, direct depth-first
evaluation therefore costs O(2^D poly(w,log n_root,D)), including the
fixed-dimensional matrix preparations. Copy the relevant ancestor path and
current header to local descriptor work. This uses a finite list of encoded
matrices, labels, widths and return state, with polynomial bit length. The
child must not fetch descriptors from a buried parking stack or from U.

As in PR2171/2188, impose the root stopping relation

    n_root <= E0,  D <= c(1+log2 E0),  w=ceil(E0^s), 0<s<1 fixed.

Then 2^D and the preparation terms are polynomial in w; division by q^w
in the complete-fibre estimate absorbs them into a uniform constant.
Use n_root here, not the much smaller current child width. For unrelated
w and D, retain E_max explicitly. We establish no selected numerical
constant for this absorption or the outer routing invoice.

## 5. Parent buffers and the existing parking boundary

PR2195 supplies a complete low packet of volume v=V/(W N_q), where
W=28416 and N_q=|GL64(F_q)|. Its unused U field contains the smaller child's
row reserve after exposing the parent high matrix. The child must receive
that entire high-by-U packet, including inactive atoms and spectators.
Parking the high matrix only as metadata would not satisfy this condition.

Use the following phase discipline for the caller. Retain its W original
family streams. Allocate separate packet buffers for the private centre,
source extraction, target extraction and route output. Complete and clear
split scratch before any recursive child boundary. Merge a returned target
into its original family only after its address calls finish. If a merge
uses a second full-family output, finish that scan before another child.
This needs at most four additional occupied packet buffers at a boundary.
Move the active packet into child I/O; keep the original centre source among
the parked buffers. During a low-class invocation, the selected literal
program has nine COPY/ERASE episodes per orientation, at most one open
private copy, 527 interior ADDs and no interior MOVE events. We check this
inventory from the pinned programs.

At a boundary, take B=W+4 marked role streams, allowing empty spare roles.
Their total occupied length is at most

    V_buf <= V+4v.

The active packet has length v. The existing PR1379 boundary theorem for
unequal lengths gives wrapper cost

    5 V_buf - v + 9 B - 2 <= 5V+19v+9B-2,

excluding the child, marker lifecycle, local descriptor copying and the
specified extraction/reinsertion scans. Those extra operations retain
separate linear or preparation charges. Do not use PR1379's equal-length
14V corollary for these unequal family and packet buffers.

Before descent, save return state and copy the child's permitted descriptor
summary into its local work. Require the child to visit no parking cell
below its entry delimiter, write no parked prefix, restore the parking and
descriptor heads, and supply a time bound uniform in ancestor contents and
stack position. Endpoint restoration alone is insufficient, as PR1379's
ancestor-scan counterexample proves. After return, restore parked originals
and replace only the active packet. The centre's transported-source ERASE
guard remains meaningful because its original source did not change.

At fixed q, the number of low classes and coarse calls is fixed. Thus these
parent wrappers add C(q)V per node while children retain volume v. They
need no new row divisor. This is a selected application of a known boundary
theorem, conditional on the child and descriptor conventions. We have not
compiled the entire selected caller or rerun a Lean machine proof. PR1641
supplies a related machine wrapper; we do not reuse its bit-flip example's
constant as a general child bound.

## 6. Evidence and remaining contracts

We compare eight complete 128-coordinate operators across four selected
fixtures, including Good/FallbackPair ancestors, against direct B_j M B_j^-1
matrices. Each retains all 16,256 shear slots. We also compare full payloads
for a three-header line over Z/9 with four address atoms and for a Z/3 case
with eight address atoms. The tests include unused stock, gap fields, opaque
record labels and exact output coverage. The first executes 1,338,444 bits;
the second executes 85,293 bits and includes paid orientation reversals.

These programs use sequential ADD/sign adapters and explicit exact F_a
oracles for the remaining completed children. We record every oracle's
width and full logical volume. Its random-access permutation model is test
instrumentation, not a physical child implementation. The selected two-atom
physical fixtures likewise do not enumerate the complete GL64 header fibre
or the full selected address array.

For the selected mixed path, a current coefficient reads A[43]. The two
ancestor substitutions give -1/11=9 modulo25; low-only ancestry gives24.
Both paths drive the physical ADD test, and we compare against the expected
record permutation. Other controls reject final-pi substitution, the wrong
upper-shear orientation and omission of one required reversal child.

We leave the general selected local-frame provider, completed weighted
children and leaf binding, the full descriptor/caller implementation and
finite routing admission open. The complex supplier and analytic transfer
remain separate obligations for integer multiplication. We prepared the
written proof and certificates with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance;
we claim no independent human or proof-assistant verification.
